I found this topic interesting and made a theorycraft for the boomkin talent tree.
Do you think the below changes would help?
I give my reasoning for every change I made.

https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/OhVxO-NNto

1. Balance of All Things
I found the original unreliable, specially for DoTs which are usually not spammed left and right.
Wanted to give a stackable buff instead (or two in this case). In the short term, they increase damage done. After the third stack, you get a free DoT.
Can be played strategically: you either swap between nature and balance to keep up the damage buffs as long as you can or you go for free and consistent DoT upkeep.
This is incredibly consistent with the nature of balance druid and the meme of moonfire spam.

Let's spin that idea further:
  • I imagine spamming moonfire could also change spell schools between arcane & fire (sun) each time you use the spell
  • Insect Swarm getting stacked would make more sense as you add more insects in a literal way right?! :D maybe it is even increasing the debuff effect of insect swarm to reduce chance of hit by 2%/3%/4% which is useful for some trash and bosses (maybe a deminishing return should be applied per stack so boomies aren't forced to keep it up all the time)

2. Eclipse
The problem is the fishing nature of it you've described.
Turned it into a resistance decreaser + spell crit giver.
My reasoning is that a spec requiring two schools of nature to be consistent has to have a way to deal with mobs having some resists. Specially since no curse exists for nature.
Moonkins also want a bunch of spellcrit. Aura gives 3% but it's really low compared what others can get.
This can be maintained by one boomkin, swapping between nature and arcane spells or by several boomkins, making sure the target gets hit by both schools of nature periodically.
I welcome the idea of Eclipse being turned into a passive effect that is applied to the target. This even underpins the support nature and could also benefit other classes like Shaman and could even give Nature Ele a boost.
Most importantly it does changes the nature of being forced into a rotation with the current state of Eclipse which goes completely against the idea of being a flexible hybrid. One of the worst things about Eclipse is to be forced to cast Starfire in encounters or phases that are movement heavy.

As there might be a strong following of the Eclipse playstyle(s):
It could also take the form of different specializations similar to arms warrior weapon specializations. Imagine being able to choose between a more active vs passive playstyle.

I believe there was a similar way starting to establish itself in WoD but Eclipse stayed a standard?

The reason behind these change ideas:
1. Wanted to give buffs which feel rewarding and not punishing like the current ones.
2. Wanted to make the effects more reliable.
3. Wanted to smuggle in some spell penetration and spell crit.

PS: These changes wouldn't make casting DoTs redundant as you frequently want them from the beginning of a fight, not after 3 casts of both wrath and starfire.
I absolutely love those ideas. Most importantly it moves the needle to a more wholesome class design. However, I'd still argue to remove Eclipse even as a spell or debuff name but maybe that's just me.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: This is What Druids really need
content_md:
I’ve been thinking about a way to give druids a clearer sense of visual progression without any heavy changes to the game, and without trying to match your form to every single gear piece. The idea is to make Bear and Cat forms feel like they “grow up” with your character in a few clean steps, kind of like Diablo, where hitting certain milestones gives you that instant “I’m stronger now” feeling.

The concept would be **purely cosmetic** and tied to broad stat thresholds. Bear form would evolve based on **Armor**, since that’s the clearest indicator of tank progression and fits the fantasy of becoming tougher and heavier over time. Cat form would evolve based on **Attack Power**, since it directly represents feral damage progression and fits the class fantasy naturally. The important part is that this wouldn’t change constantly—only when you reach meaningful milestones.

Visually, it doesn’t need a brand-new model every time. It could be **4–5 tiers max**, with changes that are subtle but instantly readable. For Bear, think a slightly bulkier silhouette, thicker fur, a more pronounced mane, maybe a few scars or druidic markings, and small primitive details like charms or runes that still feel “Vanilla” instead of flashy. For Cat, same idea: over time it looks more seasoned and more dangerous, but it’s still clearly a cat form, still grounded, and still in line with Turtle’s vibe.

On the technical side, this can be kept straightforward. When you shapeshift, the server checks your effective **Armor in Bear** or your effective **Attack Power in Cat**, then picks the cosmetic tier for that form. Because the tiers are broad, it won’t flip back and forth from small gear swaps. And to avoid forcing anyone into it, it should be **optional** via a simple toggle (NPC option, glyph-style toggle, or setting), so players who prefer the classic look can keep it permanently.

I think this fits Turtle’s direction because it’s a **flavor win with zero balance impact**. It gives druids a visible “I’ve advanced” moment that isn’t just numbers, without dragging the game toward a fashion system. Turtle already experiments with form cosmetics, so this would feel like a natural extension rather than something out of place.

The main concerns also feel manageable. If some players don’t want extra readability in PvP, keep it opt-in or easy to disable. If breakpoints are a worry, keep the number of tiers low and the thresholds wide. And if anyone’s afraid it could look too flashy, that’s just art direction—keep it primal and druidic, more “seasoned beast” than “glowing armor cat.”

If people like the idea, it could expand to other forms later, but even just Bear and Cat would already add a lot of identity and progression for druids.

author: Captain4k
subject: Hybrid Revive for the Hybrid Class
content_md:
This post is a part 2 solution to my [Give Druids a Revive Spell](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=20827) thread.

I recently came up with an idea to give Druids a classic+ revive spell that still respects vanilla design philosophy. My idea is to hybridize the [Rebirth] spell by giving it dual functionality. It would keep its reagent cost and would be usable both inside and outside of combat. If used while in combat, the spell is a 3 second cast (meaning it can be silenced or interrupted) and has a 30 min cooldown. If used outside of combat, it has a regular cast time of 10 seconds with no cooldown, but a heavy mana cost.

This is the spell's original vanilla tooltip:
![Image](https://i.postimg.cc/28G9VCrn/Screenshot-2026-01-13-at-3-20-18-PM.png)

My updated spell description would look something like this:
![Image](https://i.postimg.cc/FHN6FG8N/Chat-GPT-Image-Jan-13-2026-04-33-56-PM.png)
This change respects the overall theme of the druid and its hybrid class identity in the vanilla world. It also stays consistent with the other hybrid class, shamans, who have their own dual revive ability to rez other people as well as themselves. So this druid version would allow the revival of teammates both inside and outside of combat with adequate consequences for both.

Looking for community feedback. How do you guys feel about my hybrid solution? Why or why not?

Let me know your thoughts in the comments.

content_md:
I fully agree with this suggestion.
In my opinion, this change does not provide any unfair advantage nor does it harm game balance. It’s purely a quality-of-life improvement that makes gameplay smoother for Druids without altering class identity or the Classic+ philosophy of Turtle WoW.
The spell already exists in the game, and this proposal simply makes its usage more practical while keeping reasonable limitations in place (mana cost, cooldown, cast restrictions, reagents, etc.). It doesn’t make Druids overpowered compared to other classes — it just reduces unnecessary friction in situations where the ability is already intended to be useful.
Most importantly, this kind of change improves overall group comfort, especially in longer dungeons or recovery situations, without trivializing content or removing meaningful decision-making.
Overall, this feels like a sensible and well-thought-out quality-of-life improvement that benefits everyone while staying true to the spirit of the game.
+1 from me.

subject: Re: Hybrid Revive for the Hybrid Class
content_md: I have no problem with Druid healers getting a normal, unrestricted rez — but Turtle WoW has had years to do so, and has not done so, despite continuous player pleading that a normal rez is part of the minimum workable toolkit for healers.  Rightly or wrongly Turtle views handing us a normal rez to be too much class homogenization.  I don’t think more years of the same discussion are likely to change their view.  But perhaps we can find a rez solution that has a different flavor/mechanic — enough to reduce the class homogenization concern

author: Terrydavis
subject: Re: Druid leveling tips
content_md:
when you tank a dungeon make sure to equip all the stuff with the most stamina it makes healing you a lot easier so you can make more mistakes

bracer +9 stamina enchant only costs 1 gold and there arent a lot of bracers in the game. some of them you can wear for 20+ levels.
(cloak +70 armor is only 60s silver but the other stuff mentioned here is more money efficient)
armor kits from leather working are also all under 1g, i think its worth it to put on some good rares. especially rares from newly added dungeons since some of these are stupid op

some of the newly added dungeons are extremely long for their level so you might want to befriend some healers who wont leave in the middle of them.

make sure to play dungeons fast, everyone likes that and people will get angry at time waster tanks

for solo leveling stamina is not important at all so you might want to keep 2 gear sets

before you reach lvl 40 only learn the skills you need! this is very important or you will go to 0 money.

i havent played druid in a while so other people can help you more with that
fairy fire lvl 1 is good enough for pulling
you also want to skill the healing over time and start hard packs and bosses with your own HOT on you

author: Chev03
subject: Re: Druid leveling tips
content_md:
****Here is a couple of useful tips for your druid endeavor****   satisfied_turtle_head

 **Macro Spells** For each of your physical attacks I recommend to make a macro like this. It triggers an autoattack before the ability and will auto target the closest enemy in front of you. It's a basic for every melee. Code: Select all

```
/startattack
/cast Swipe
```

For talents:
 - **Thick Hide:** don't forget to spec into for the extra Armor. Healers will thank you and its generally useful. Many cat druids are squishy for missing out on it or forgetting to upgrade their items
 - **Nature's Grasp:** in Balance is worth one point for the escape utility
 - **Sylvan Blessing:** if you need to heal yourself often or if you catch yourself drinking after getting bear form, consider a single point
 - **Feral Instinct:** One point should be enough in the beginning - put more in only if you struggle with holding aggro

On lower levels I play like this to speed things up:
 - range pull 2-3 mobs with a DoT like Moonfire or Insect Swarm
 - switch to Bear and Swipe to cleave em down

Here is a light talent suggestion to start:
<https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/druid?points=BB-FAJYRQ->

Make it your own and adapt to how you play like

author: Captain4k
subject: Re: Druid leveling tips
content_md:
> **Nuninho32 wrote: Mon Jan 19, 2026 2:06 pm**
> Hello turtles, im planning on leveling a druid and i have a few questions that i need some opinion. Any advice and tips are appreciated :)

As a tank main (Bear, paladin, warrior) since 2008, here's my opinion.

I 100% agree with this:
> **Chev03 wrote: Wed Jan 21, 2026 9:46 am**
> ***Macro Spells for each of your physical attacks. I recommend to make a macro like this. It triggers an auto-attack before the ability and will auto target the closest enemy in front of you.*** Code: Select all
>
> ```
> /startattack
> /cast Swipe
> ```

But he forgot to mention that you need addons such as "****CleveRoid Macros****" in order for these macro inputs to work in the vanilla 1.12 client.

> 1- Night Elf or Tauren ?

For tanking, Tauren is always the better option due to their racial ability that grants 5% extra Stamina, which are tanks most important stat. Tauren also have a much bigger bear form model than night elves. So it adds to the immersion of the tank fantasy.

> 2-  I want to level up as feral and tank dungeons at the same time, can you give me a talent build?

[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/druid?po ... DQQIFQB-Ao](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/druid?points=BSAaAI-FAYYRaDQQIFQB-Ao)
This is the meta tank build for the current patch of class changes. A lot of people ignore [Sylvan Blessing] because it is worded weirdly. But it's a really important talent that helps keep you from going out of mana when you heal yourself in between mobs. This minimizes your down time, so you don't have to stop and drink often while leveling.

> 3- Omen of clarity and Furor first or go straight full feral ?

Always go [Omen of Clarity] first by Lv20, then into [Furor] by Lv25. The clearcasting procs very often and gives you tons of threat when tanking from all the free swipes you get in bear form. It also gives you free claws/shreds in cat form, so you kill targets faster while questing and maximize your up time. These two talents provide a much smoother and more efficient leveling experience.

author: Sleeplust
subject: Tiger's Fury in 2026 ≈ Savage Roar in 2008 = Technically Unskillful Design
content_md:
To begin with, savage roar in WotLK is a clumsy skill, which significantly enhances the user's all phisical damage by 30% without a cooldown. The issue is that this skill, just like ferocious bite, consumes combo points while all other melee attacks require savage roar to be activated for efficiency. In other words, the design involves a weakened set of basic skills that need to be enhanced by using savage roar. To illustrate that, a feral druid's maximised ferocious bite and rip must land on the target before savage roar's effect elapses, which means that the druid needs to make five combo points, confirm rake's bleeding effect, land a rip or ferocious bite and make at least one combo point for the next savage roar. All these must be done in about 35 seconds. If you fail that, you are considered under-geared or incompetent. That was a time of inconvenience and frustration, no matter how high the DPS could be, because the loop of skills was relatively more complicated and difficult to sustain. I dislike this skill and it deepens my disfavour of the whole expansion.

In the later expansion Cataclysm, the effect of savage roar is optimised into increasing only automatic non-skill melee damage, but that still blindly complicates the mechanism as most damaging skills are influenced so players still need to cover the loop with savage roar for efficiency.

Back to TWoW's discussion, the name savage roar has never existed in TWoW, but Tiger's Fury (in early 2026) is the de facto savage roar skill, with a zero-cooldown and nearly universal enhancement for other melee skills of cat form.

How can designers modify or replace the current tiger's fury mechanism? A possible change is making this skill more like its WotLK version, adding an instant energy recovery with a long cooldown. Also, the attack boost from using the skill should be replaced with a passive attack increase merged into the basic panel data.

By comparison, warlock's Improve Soulfire talent is scientically much more acceptable. Why? Unlike savage roar and tiger's fury, soulfire itself deals great damage and it has a long cooldown. The universal damage boost only applies on fire damage. Equally importantly, the enhancement functions even if soulfire fails to land. As a destruction warlock, I feel casting soulfire a natural, amusing and persuasive choice. It returns a soul shard and never consumes precious combo points and energy - it can be casted without preparation and no wait is needed before casting following damage, like immolate and conflagrate.

author: Wosator
subject: Devs hate Druids?
content_md:
So I've been playing feral druid for quite some time. I've spend many hours trying to perfect my bindings, macros etc, I got almost BIS gear, other than a couple of items for PVP, and still I get completely and absolutely crushed by certain classes.

I will share 4 cases as case studies on events that happened to me today, doing outdoor pvp.

Case 1 - VS Ele/ Enh Tank Shaman

So I found this guy, he had good gear, but not better than mine. He had 5k+ hp, and so did i (with buffs).

I opened the fight and i did a crit shred on him. I did 350dmg, again and again, even with rake and rip on my dmg was simply pathetic. You'd think ok, he is a tank and that's fair, but then let's go to the damage HE did on me. The fight took roughly 15 seconds, he casted 3 earth shocks on me all three crits averaging 1800 EACH. 0 skill, just pure insanity. It's like fighting 3vs1. Then the dude proceeded to kill some elite, even though i never attack someone that is not full hp or in a fight, i went for it, and surely he just melted both me and the elite no issues, he was still above 70% hp...

Case 2 - VS Assassination Rogue

I opened him, did shred crit of about 1k, before he could do any dmg on me i got him to 50%, then he kidney shotted me, i trinketed, eventually i killed him, but he got me to 30% hp in less than 5 seconds. Latest patch supposedly nerfed the stupidly broken poisons, but in fact, they got buffed. Dissolvent poisons used to hit me for about 200, now instant poisons hit me 220-250/hit and he hits like crazy, its like 700dps from poisons only.

Case 3 - VS Demo/Affliction lock

I opened him, he coiled me, he didn't even bother to fear me, just 3 dots and until coil was over, and i run back to him, i was dead, even with Zanza and pot. His dots tick for about 600/tick + soul drain its like 1000 dps. Then he /w me from another character telling me that I am noob because i could heal and decurse... I mean you can't make this shit up.. his Agony was ticking for 130dmg not worth going in and out of cat form to decurse because the whole fight took 5 seconds. It's just impossible not only to kill, but to get him to 50% even when i open, and even then he didn't even bothered to sacrifice Void, or use healthstone, and he still had soulstone on.

Then a hunter saw the fight and joined, the lock killed him as well, and he was still above 50% hp without sacrificing Void...

Case 4 - VS Discipline Priest

This happened in AB, i open him, get him to 50%. All he had to do was jump around spamming holy nova, and insta smites. I was dead within 5 sec, he did x2 crit insta Smites for 1400 each + the holy novas.

All these classes got insanely broken buffs, while feral druids are getting nerf after nerf after nerf, even thought they completely underwhelmingly underpowered. In order for me to do proper dps on them, i need to play litteral piano building dots, and hopping for all the starts to align and even then the best i can hope for is to get them to 50% hp? With all of their CDs still untapped?

Even Shred, which is the most powerful ability I have is completely crap when compared to any of their abilities, not to talk about skills like savage bite, which should rather be named kitty's cuddle. It cost 25 rage, and does what 300dmg (today i **critted** an arms warrior for 141dmg with it).

Are you also equally frustrated with how miserably unbalanced PVP is and how devs keep making it worse in every patch?

author: Auralys
subject: Balance Druid still feels unrewarding and overly RNG after latest changes
content_md:
Hello,
I’m posting this as a K40-geared Balance Druid (with Scythe of Elune), and even after the recent changes to Starfire crit chances, the spec still feels really off to play.

The main issue is that the gameplay just isn’t rewarding when you play it correctly !

Right now, when an Eclipse procs, you’re often forced to stopcast the spell you just started because letting it go through is a DPS loss. Since Eclipse windows are so short, you basically have to cancel your cast and immediately switch to the buffed spell.

At the same time, you’re expected to maintain your DoTs on the target, but you have no control over Eclipse procs, which makes some 12-second windows feel almost wasted.

That means optimal gameplay = constantly interrupting yourself.
It feels clunky, unintuitive, and frustrating.

On top of that, the spec feels way too RNG-dependent. More crit just means more procs, but also more situations where you have to react instantly or lose value. You don’t really gain control over your damage, it just becomes more chaotic. Threat generation also becomes very inconsistent because of this.

At the end of the day, you’re putting in more effort than most casters for equal or lower results. And unlike others, we don’t even have a real burst cooldown to stabilize our damage or create a strong window.

Another big issue is how inconsistent procs are with Balance spells.

Moonfire and Insect Swarm ticks don’t proc trinkets (Scythe, Clackora, Sigil), and Hurricane doesn’t either. Meanwhile, other classes can proc everything very easily with instant or low-commitment abilities (Arcane Explosion or Holy Nova, for example).

This makes DoTs feel underwhelming and AoE even worse, especially considering Hurricane is already harder to use properly (channeled, positioning-dependent, and punishing if mobs move).

I recently got the Clackora trinket, and honestly it feels awful on Balance, even though it should be a strong item. Even trying to stack it with rank 1 Wrath feels extremely inconsistent and unreliable.

I don’t think the spec needs more crit. It needs more consistency.

A few changes that would already improve the feel a lot:

Let Eclipse apply to the current cast instead of forcing stopcasting
(for example: the next Wrath after an Eclipse proc benefits from Arcane Eclipse, and the next Starfire benefits from Nature Eclipse — this would feel much more fluid and rewarding)
Allow DoTs (Moonfire / Insect Swarm) and Hurricane to proc trinkets and effects
Add a meaningful cooldown to give the spec some control over its damage
(for example: a cooldown that extends the current Eclipse by ~12 seconds every 3 minutes)

 **Right now, the spec feels clunky, RNG-heavy, and less rewarding than simpler alternatives.**

Curious to hear if other Balance players feel the same, especially with raid gear and logs to compare.

Thanks for reading.

At the end of the day, you’re putting in more effort than most casters for equal or lower results. And unlike others, we don’t even have a real burst cooldown to stabilize our damage or create a strong window.

Another big issue is how inconsistent procs are with Balance spells.

Moonfire and Insect Swarm ticks don’t proc trinkets (Scythe, Clackora, Sigil), and Hurricane doesn’t either. Meanwhile, other classes can proc everything very easily with instant or low-commitment abilities (Arcane Explosion or Holy Nova, for example).

This makes DoTs feel underwhelming and AoE even worse, especially considering Hurricane is already harder to use properly (channeled, positioning-dependent, and punishing if mobs move).

I recently got the Clackora trinket, and honestly it feels awful on Balance, even though it should be a strong item. Even trying to stack it with rank 1 Wrath feels extremely inconsistent and unreliable.

I don’t think the spec needs more crit. It needs more consistency.

A few changes that would already improve the feel a lot:

Let Eclipse apply to the current cast instead of forcing stopcasting
(for example: the next Wrath after an Eclipse proc benefits from Arcane Eclipse, and the next Starfire benefits from Nature Eclipse — this would feel much more fluid and rewarding)
Allow DoTs (Moonfire / Insect Swarm) and Hurricane to proc trinkets and effects
Add a meaningful cooldown to give the spec some control over its damage
(for example: a cooldown that extends the current Eclipse by ~12 seconds every 3 minutes)

Right now, the spec feels clunky, RNG-heavy, and less rewarding than simpler alternatives.

Curious to hear if other Balance players feel the same, especially with raid gear and logs to compare.

Thanks for reading.

author: Jizzus
subject: Re: Balance Druid still feels unrewarding and overly RNG after latest changes
content_md:
As a fully BiS Ambershire Balance Druid main (aside from the newly released BWL and ES) I feel the exact same.

First of all lets discuss the elephant in the room in the form of the recent change to balance of all things. It feels awful and performs just about as awful.

For the mana reduction part of wrath I don't have any actual complaint. I can't speak from a nord perspective but from an Ambershire perspective and even with the longer fights in bwl mana isn't an issue if you have innervate, mana potions, tea/demonic rune/dark rune unless there was a chaotic fight where you were forced to both tranquility and combat ress someone and perhaps assist healing in more forms. With that being said we still have way more mana issues than any other caster.

Now the moonfire/starfire change feels absolutely dreadful and in my opinion this is why:

 1- Previously you could stack 0.5 sec reductions before a boss fight. It wasn't broken, it didn't mean we were gonna outdps any of the other casters it just gave us a bit more control over what is a very RNG dependant spec that even when all the stars align is outdpsed by a mile by every other caster while bringing very little to the whole group.

 2- Lets look at a standalone example. A lot of the times it takes you 3 maybe 4 or maybe more wraths to get a lunar eclipse. And once lunar eclipse starts realistically you are playing with a 8-9 moonfire on your target which you don't want to reapply because doing so is actually a dps loss and you'd rather spend the entirety of your lunar casting as many starfires as possible except for the last few seconds where you might want to indeed reapply  moonfire if there's not enough time left for your starfire to hit. With the previous iteration even if you had the exact same thing happen and even if you didn't start the boss fight with pre-stacks for your cast they are still stacking up as you fish for your eclipse.

The buff to moonfury was a welcome one because it's a consistent buff but at the end of the day balance druid is still fighting for spots against every other caster and giving 15% crit spread across 5 players is a dps loss for the raid compared to bringing another mage or a warlock which by the way bring their own benefits to the raid while doing a lot more damage. Mage has the same decurse and brings arcane intellect and waters and amazing aoe. Warlocks bring curse of elements and shadow, healthstones and soulstones.

I don't particularly understand the reluctance to buff the spec in a meaningful way when it's so clearly far behind everything else. If pvp could become an issue with those changes well now you have dampen so if you feel like balance druid is where it should be in pvp you buff it in pve and add a bit extra dampen to make up for it. It does seem like a poor excuse as that doesn't seem to be the case either.

But even if we took the dps aside the spec just feels unrewarding to play. In fact I'd argue crit is the opposite of what we need. We'd rather have more consistency and then if we get the ocasional big crit it feels much better.

And by the way changing balance of all things to 3 talent points... It's...nice? But the extra 2 points aren't going into anything particularly meaningful. The sheer amount of spellhit we require compared to other casters is equally atrocious. If you are afraid to leave ferals needing 0 melee hit maybe change natural weapons to give the same 3% melee hit but 10 % spell hit. And yes I am saying 10 and I do not think it's outrageous to ask for that.

Also gatekeeping some of the spec's potential behind specific tier bonuses is another bad policy. Right now on Ambershire it's Tier 2 time and guess what? The tier 2 bonuses are all inconsequential in pve.

In sum you could give us spell hit cap from talents, infinite mana and even reduce starfire cast by 0.5secs by default and not only would the spec still feel unrewarding to play but we'd probably still be behind other casters.

For my part, I quite agree with what is said above, but I would add:

For the PVE part

We are one of the rare classes that is not a single button (we have to think about the eclipse proc + refresh dots + watch out for mana + x3 buff /invervation / dispel x2 basically we have to do a lot of things and I have the impression that twow sees the boomy as a dps assist and not the dps it deserves (I have full bis t3.5 + t3 + scythe stuff and full enchant /food /flask etc) and it would be completely logical to be in the top 5 dps but I only see mages /feral /rogue / warrior and on top of that the number 1 source of damage is often auto attack or a single spam spell.

I don't want to cry at all about my class because I play boomy nerf or not and I like this class that I have been playing since wow vanilla, but I would like to have a little fun and not have to do like the whole server that is to say making a new character mage /feral /rogue /warrior.

Summary: huge lack of mono + multi /mana dps which burns faster than other classes / totally dependent on rng + eclipse and if possible do something for the Scythian but only for boomies (we specialize in nature and especially the Arcane and the Scythian should improve the boomy much more than a mage /warlock)

For the PVP part (with all these difficulties I still raised rank 14)

I would just like to say that we are crispy chips for all other twow classes, almost no survivability and kiting is very difficult with our only 36 yard max range... The same thing for arenas, I can't do it with this survivability

BIG MESSAGE FOR DEV TWOW The balancing of classes as in all games must be done in waves, that is to say that there is a rotation: a class can be number 1 dps and the next patch go to number 10 dps (only certain classes escape this) wink mage /rogue If you want more new players who play bommy listen to us or we all recreate mages /rogue and we play turtlemage /turtlerogue!

author: Froizerk
subject: The problem with T3.5 gear set bonus RDruid
content_md:
So i have been playing resto druid for quite a while, when raiding in the Upper Tier Raids i see a very obvious problem with the set bonus in whole.

 - ***Blooming Bud***
Blooming Bud why is it an issue as a set bonus? Blooming Bud is a set bonus that tries to help swiftmend do more  impact but fails. Previously when Blooming Bud had infinite linger it was a good set bonus to buff before raid to make the raid healthier. Entering the new patch blooming bud now has a 20s Linger which only realisticly effects the tanks to get the proc (240 healing once getting hit).

 - ***Blooming bud as a buff***
It being a buff makes no sense, in the current raiding phase buff slots are very limited In raids above naxx for clarity but its workaroundable.

 - ***The FIx for Blooming Bud***
The set bonus of T3.5 mostly focuses on lower Swiftmend CD for more blooming buds, considering they do little to no impact they don't work together. The solution to this would be reworking blooming bud to be something entirely else for it to work/ make blooming bud a buff thats worth having on your buff slots.

 - ***Some Blooming Bud Ideas***
Your swiftmend applies blooming bud which does an explosion vfx and heals people in a 10yard range (1200 healing power scaling needs tuning) healing split into 10yard explosion (that heals people by 1200 / people count)
 - ***Some T3.5 5set replacements***
Your rejuvenation ticks now have a 5% chance to grant you elunes favor
 1st variant Elunes favor: Increases the healing done by your next rejuvenation by 20%
 2nd variant Elunes favor: Increases the healing done by your next regrowth by 30%
(these numbers should be adjusted to the strength of druid at patch)

author: Noephix
subject: The state of druid in 1.18.1 (all 4 specs)
content_md:
**CAT**: Cat sucks because item devs made a mistake, refused to acknowledge and doubled down on it.
Cat is great dps spec at low gear levels - but in current endgame raid it's one of the worst.
Cat doesn't get a big full-slot item upgrade in Naxx, unlike literally every other DPS spec. But for some reason items devs thought that it did and designed cat gear in Kara40 to be only slightly better than it's previous BiS (which is basically AQ4 gear with ~3 Naxx items), resulting in Kara40 cat gear having tons of dump stats (roughly over 50% of stat budget) and cats falling far behind on gearing (since Naxx is the highest jump in item quality through the entire game). Then they attempted to fix it by buffing cat's talents, resulting in cat becoming OP DPS during AQ40 (cause that's where al the good cat gear comes from) while still falling off a cliff in Kara40.

Also unsuccessful attempts at fixing cat dps resulted in bleed rotation coming into existence, which deals more damage than oldschool powershifting but many bosses are immune to it, so cats end up spreading skill points between 2 specs and having not enough for any optional/QoL talents, resulting in those talents being dead. Cat needs to be lvl 62 to take all the mandatory DPS talents without a single flex point. Too bad lvl cap is 60.

 **BEAR**: bear sucks because threat was the only thing going for them and now it's gone.
Bear mitigation sucks. Bears take over 2x the damage while having only around ~20% more HP than warriors. Extra damage comes from the fact that bear can't parry or block and is a subject to crits and crushing blows (which isn't something that happens to a half-competent warrior or paladin tank). Bear snap threat is way worse than paladin's, while threat over time isn't really an issue for most tanks, be it warrior, pala or bear (not sure about shamans). Now there's literally no reason to bring a bear tank over warrior or paladin.

Also item devs strike once again, making bear t3 choke-full of useless and low-value stats like intellect or defense (bear cant parry or block, remember?). So the best current bear set in game by far is.... PvP t3. Because pvp sets are naturally made with proper stats. Yes, bears have to spend months upon months on BGs to get their pve BiS set.

 **MOONKIN**: Moonkin sucks because the math isn't mathing. Yeah, the rotation is kinda fun (even if some people object), items are OK - but the numbers are just too low. 1.18.1 moonkin rework was supposed to be a slight buff - but ended up being ~15% dps nerf to already low-tier spec, resulting in moonkin becoming the worst "proper" dps spec in the game. Below even cat. Also talent overload is a problem once again, too many mandatory talents.

 **RESTORATION**: resto sucks because there's only 1 slot for a resto druid in 40-man raid. Maybe 2, if they coordinate. But more than 2 - and they start griefing each other by overwriting each other's heals. Dev team's attempts to fix the problem didn't really help.
And resto also sucks because holy priest does resto's "speciality" (heal over time) much better.

Now there's literally no reason to bring a bear tank over warrior or paladin.

Also item devs strike once again, making bear t3 choke-full of useless and low-value stats like intellect or defense (bear cant parry or block, remember?). So the best current bear set in game by far is.... PvP t3. Because pvp sets are naturally made with proper stats. Yes, bears have to spend months upon months on BGs to get their pve BiS set.

MOONKIN: Moonkin sucks because the math isn't mathing. Yeah, the rotation is kinda fun (even if some people object), items are OK - but the numbers are just too low. 1.18.1 moonkin rework was supposed to be a slight buff - but ended up being ~15% dps nerf to already low-tier spec, resulting in moonkin becoming the worst "proper" dps spec in the game. Below even cat. Also talent overload is a problem once again, too many mandatory talents.

RESTORATION: resto sucks because there's only 1 slot for a resto druid in 40-man raid. Maybe 2, if they coordinate. But more than 2 - and they start griefing each other by overwriting each other's heals. Dev team's attempts to fix the problem didn't really help.
And resto also sucks because holy priest does resto's "speciality" (heal over time) much better.
